jobs.title: Will AI replace journalists? What the evidence shows
jobs.desc: Graded, dated evidence on what AI can and can't do in journalism: routine stories, drafting, summarising news, fact-checking, and the job numbers.

bls.outlook: -6% (-2,800 jobs), 2025-35. BLS cites falling advertising revenue in radio, newspapers and TV and newsroom consolidation, partly offset by demand for online news. The page does not mention AI.
bls.label: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook

jobs.verdict: Newsrooms have automated formulaic stories for a decade and most staff at some outlets now use AI daily, and a few publishers have tied layoffs partly to AI. But AI still distorts news when it summarises it and has put invented books and quotes into print. BLS projects decline, which it blames on advertising and consolidation, not AI.

tasks.evidence: AP automated corporate earnings stories, going from about 300 a quarter to 3,700; it said automation freed about 20% of staff time and did not cut jobs.
tasks.label: Journalism.co.uk, Jun 2015

tasks.evidence: Business Insider said over 70% of its employees use Enterprise ChatGPT, with a goal of 100%, as it went 'all-in on AI'.
tasks.label: Nieman Lab, May 2025

tasks.evidence: BBC journalists found 51% of answers from ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and Perplexity to 100 news questions had significant issues.
tasks.label: Digital Content Next, Feb 2025

tasks.evidence: The Chicago Sun-Times and Philadelphia Inquirer ran a syndicated AI-generated summer reading list recommending books that don't exist; the freelancer said he 'failed' to check the chatbot's output.
tasks.label: eWeek, May 2025

jobs_evidence: Business Insider cuts 21% of staff; CEO memo cites 'extreme traffic drops outside of our control' and says 'we are going all-in on AI' (company says AI, in part)

E.W. Scripps cuts 268 jobs across about a dozen local TV stations as it shifts to streaming; reporters describe an 'AI-powered' newsroom model, but no Scripps quote directly ties the cuts to AI (reported as AI)
GB News proposes up to 90 job cuts as it introduces automated production workflows (company says automation)
Microsoft's AI-applicability study puts news analysts, reporters and journalists among the 40 most AI-applicable occupations (study)
what_to_do: Do the reporting AI can't
Original sourcing, interviews and being on the scene are what AI summaries depend on and cannot produce.
Verify everything AI touches
AI has put invented books and quotes into print. Newsrooms need people who check every name, figure and quote.
Use AI for the grunt work
Transcription, first drafts of routine items and data processing free time for enterprise stories, as AP found with earnings reports.
Build a direct audience
Publishers cite search-traffic drops as much as AI itself. Journalists with their own following are less exposed.
faq: Will AI replace journalists?
Not wholesale. BLS projects a 6% decline for 2025-35 but blames advertising and consolidation; a few publishers, such as Business Insider, have cited AI as part of the reason for cuts.
Can AI write news stories?
It has written formulaic earnings stories at AP since about 2014. For broader news, AI assistants still distort or misattribute facts in about half of answers, according to a 2025 BBC study.
Which newsrooms have cut jobs over AI?
Business Insider (21%) cited AI along with traffic losses, GB News cited automated workflows, and coverage of Scripps' cuts describes an AI-powered model.
What journalism tasks are safest?
Original reporting, investigations, interviews and verification.

jobs.title: Will AI replace HR and recruiters? What the evidence shows
jobs.desc: Graded, dated evidence on what AI can and can't do in HR and recruiting: employee questions, résumé screening, interviews, and the job numbers.

bls.outlook: +6% (+60,100 jobs), 2025-35, faster than average. BLS expects strong demand and more HR work outsourced to HR-services firms. The page does not mention AI.
bls.label: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook

jobs.verdict: HR is one of the first corporate functions where a big company has said plainly that AI replaced staff: IBM cut a few hundred HR roles after its HR chatbot began resolving most routine questions. AI also screens résumés and, in one large experiment, ran first-round interviews well. BLS still projects growth, and AI screening is now the subject of a discrimination lawsuit.

tasks.evidence: IBM says its AskHR agent resolves 94% of common questions without a human, automates around 80 HR tasks and handled more than 11.5 million interactions in 2024 (company figures).
tasks.label: IBM, Aug 2025

tasks.evidence: A federal judge let an age-discrimination collective action proceed against Workday, whose AI tools score, sort and rank applicants for employers; Workday says the suit lacks merit.
tasks.label: Holland & Knight, May 2025

tasks.evidence: In a field experiment with about 70,000 applicants, AI voice-agent interviews raised job offers 12%, starts 18% and 30-day retention 17%; human recruiters still made every hiring decision.
tasks.label: Marginal Revolution on Jabarian & Henkel, Sep 2025

tasks.evidence: Even IBM's CEO, while predicting routine HR tasks would be fully automated, said HR work such as assessing workforce composition and productivity would be unaffected for about ten years.
tasks.label: Neowin, May 2023

jobs_evidence: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna tells the WSJ IBM eliminated a few hundred HR roles using AI, while 'our total employment has actually gone up' (company says AI)

IBM says it will slow or pause hiring for back-office roles, with HR hit hardest; Krishna: 'I could easily see 30% of that getting replaced by AI and automation over a five-year period' (company says AI)
Amazon cuts about 14,000 corporate jobs; earlier reports said human resources was among targets, and CEO Andy Jassy had written that AI 'will reduce our total corporate workforce' (reported as AI)
what_to_do: Move up from transactional HR
Benefits questions, verification letters and transfers are the tasks IBM automated first. Employee relations, investigations and workforce planning are holding up.
Learn to audit hiring AI
With the Workday lawsuit proceeding, employers need people who can test screening tools for bias and explain their decisions.
Use AI interviewers carefully
Research shows AI first-round interviews can work, but humans still make the hire. Own the judgment step.
Consider HR-services firms
BLS expects outsourced HR providers to grow faster than in-house departments.
faq: Will AI replace HR specialists?

Not on current evidence for the occupation overall. BLS projects 6% growth (+60,100 jobs) for 2025-35 and does not mention AI, but routine HR service roles are being automated at some large employers.
Has any company replaced HR staff with AI?
Yes. IBM's CEO said in 2025 that it eliminated a few hundred HR roles using AI, while hiring elsewhere.
Is AI résumé screening legal?
It is legal but contested. A federal court let an age-discrimination collective action against Workday's AI screening proceed in 2025; the case is ongoing.
Do candidates mind AI interviews?
In one large experiment, 78% of applicants offered the choice picked the AI interviewer, and AI-interviewed candidates got more offers.
